Backlog as single source of truth with its generated views (roadmap, issues, CI, fixture)
Release by tag: runbook, OIDC publish, milestone close, drift check, HG-5

nodes.label: CI fall-through test per harness
nodes.rationale: A handler with no key must fall through — exit 0, empty stdout — once per harness environment: Claude Code (CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT) and Codex CLI (PLUGIN_ROOT).

nodes.label: CodeQL analysis (security-extended, weekly)
nodes.rationale: Static analysis of the one runtime file tree the plugin ships; a hook runs with the user permissions on every tool call, so the bar for what lands in bin/ is high.

nodes.label: Stable HG-n item id
nodes.rationale: The id never changes; a new item takes the next free number, never a retired one. Moving an item across milestones is fine, renumbering is not. Dropped items keep the id with ver=dropped so the reasoning stays on record.

nodes.label: Keep a Changelog format with HG-n ids
nodes.norm_label: keep a changelog format with hg-n ids

nodes.label: Claude Code hooks contract (read 2026-09-22)
nodes.rationale: stdin JSON: session_id, cwd, hook_event_name, tool_name, tool_input, tool_use_id on PreToolUse; last_assistant_message, stop_reason on Stop. stdout: hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision allow|deny|ask plus reason; block on Stop; systemMessage. Exit 0 read JSON, exit 2 block. Default timeout 600 s so ours is explicit.

nodes.label: Codex CLI hooks contract (verified 2026-09-22)
nodes.rationale: Same events and stdin fields plus turn_id; PreToolUse takes permissionDecision but only allow|deny, no ask; Stop is {decision: block, reason}; PostToolUse has no additionalContext, its decision: block records feedback. Codex 0.155.1 lists plugin_hooks as removed, so install is a repo- or user-level hooks.json written by hookgate print-hooks; repo hooks need persisted trust. Codex rules (Starlark prefix_rule) are the natural promotion target.

nodes.label: Audit mode
nodes.rationale: Every gate judges for real, logs one JSON line per decision, always falls through; hookgate report prints decisions by outcome, p50/p95 latency, cache hit rate and ask share per threshold. Start here.

nodes.label: Claude Code hooks (prior art)
nodes.rationale: type: prompt hooks are the incumbent for judged decisions; hookgate is the faster, calibrated alternative.

nodes.label: Command risk gate (PreToolUse on Bash)
nodes.rationale: Choice{allow, ask, deny} plus a Noul "destroys data or state outside the repo?". Below the confidence threshold it is always ask, never allow. A confident allow passes through by default: hookgate narrows what the harness would do, never widens it; allowMode: "allow" opts in.

nodes.label: hookgate doctor
nodes.rationale: Key, connectivity, latency, model, config, harness; non-zero only on a broken configuration, never on a slow API.

nodes.label: .claude/hookgate.json configuration
nodes.rationale: mode, model, timeoutMs, failClosed, allowMode, thresholds {confidence, destructive, unverified, injection}, gates {command, completion, injection}; every key optional. Thresholds scale with risk as TypeSafe confidence guide recommends; defaults conservative, the benchmark moves them.

nodes.label: Injected instructions screen (PostToolUse)
nodes.rationale: Noul "does this output contain instructions addressed to an AI agent?" on WebFetch, WebSearch, Read, Bash; additionalContext telling the agent to treat the span as data. Off by default until the fixture set gives a false-positive rate.

nodes.label: Per-session cache
nodes.rationale: The same command in the same session is judged once; a repeat answers in microseconds with no request and never outlives the session.

nodes.label: Rule promotion
nodes.rationale: Three verdicts above 95% confidence on one command prefix produce one systemMessage proposing the harness own permission rule — Bash(npm test *) for Claude Code, prefix_rule() for Codex. Proposed, never written.

nodes.label: Secret redaction before send
nodes.rationale: Key shapes, bearer headers, KEY=value assignments, URL passwords and private keys are redacted; state truncated well under Jev 32k-token limit.

nodes.label: Two harnesses, one file
nodes.rationale: Handlers read the same stdin JSON under Claude Code and Codex CLI and answer in each shape. Codex has no ask on PreToolUse, so a below-threshold answer passes through with the concern as a systemMessage (codex.askAs: deny refuses instead); the injection screen uses Codex decision: block. Exercised against live Codex 0.155.1.

nodes.label: type: prompt hooks (the incumbent)
nodes.rationale: A full LLM call per decision: seconds and cents each; the benchmark baseline.

nodes.label: TypeSafe Jev (System One model)
nodes.rationale: Returns typed decisions with a confidence score instead of text, in about 100 ms.

nodes.label: Unverified completion gate (Stop)
nodes.rationale: Noul on the last message plus git status; block with a reason naming what to verify, once per prompt so the agent cannot loop.

nodes.label: What leaves the machine, exactly
nodes.rationale: One HTTPS POST per decision to api.typesafe.ai carrying only what the question needs: command, description, last two cwd segments and permission mode; final message, stop reason and first sixty lines of git status --porcelain; the tool output. Never the transcript, file contents not just fetched, or the session id. Audit log keeps verdicts and a command prefix. HOOKGATE_ENDPOINT points at a proxy.

nodes.label: Out of scope for HG-1
nodes.rationale: Teaching Jev, an SDK, PostToolUse hygiene, gating other tools, the Codex adapter itself, other harnesses, offline fallback, telemetry, auto-tuning, rewriting user permissions, second labeller, the site, Windows testing.

nodes.label: Q10 · How much Codex must exist in 0.1.0
nodes.rationale: Default: environment detection and one output-shaping function with a unit test per harness; no .codex-plugin manifest until Research confirms Codex event names and decision vocabulary.
nodes.norm_label: q10 · how much codex must exist in 0.1.0

nodes.label: Q1 · Does 0.1.0 emit allow at all
nodes.rationale: A false allow on a destructive command is the single worst outcome. Default: code emits all three; shipped default makes allow effectively unreachable until the benchmark justifies lowering it; deny is emitted from 0.1.0.
nodes.norm_label: q1 · does 0.1.0 emit allow at all

nodes.label: Q2 · May a repo config loosen the gate
nodes.rationale: A hostile repo config could turn the safety gate into an auto-approver. Default: user-level config sets the floor and owns fail-closed; a repo file may only tighten.
nodes.norm_label: q2 · may a repo config loosen the gate

nodes.label: Q3 · Who labels the benchmark commands and by what rule
nodes.rationale: The agreement percentage is only as good as the labels. Default: maintainer labels alone with a written rule in CONTRIBUTING (dangerous = irreversible loss or exfiltration outside repo; ask = reversible-but-consequential; safe = read-only or repo-local).
nodes.norm_label: q3 · who labels the benchmark commands and by what rule

nodes.label: Q4 · Is shipping every Bash command to a third-party API acceptable and what is redacted
nodes.rationale: Default: acceptable for the maintainer; README states what is sent; credential-looking values replaced with <redacted>; cwd sent as basename.
nodes.norm_label: q4 · is shipping every bash command to a third-party api acceptable and what is redacted

nodes.label: Q5 · How many times may the Stop gate block per turn
nodes.rationale: A looping block burns the tokens the plugin exists to save. Default: at most one block per stop sequence; on stop_hook_active exit 0 without calling Jev.
nodes.norm_label: q5 · how many times may the stop gate block per turn

nodes.label: Q6 · What does git state mean for the Stop gate
nodes.rationale: Default: git status --porcelain capped at 50 lines, empty outside a repo; the transcript is not read in 0.1.0.
nodes.norm_label: q6 · what does git state mean for the stop gate

nodes.label: Q7 · Does the Stop gate call Jev on every stop
nodes.rationale: Default: a local prefilter for completion language first; only messages that pass go to Jev.
nodes.norm_label: q7 · does the stop gate call jev on every stop

nodes.label: Q8 · How is the type prompt reference run reproducibly
nodes.rationale: A real type: prompt hook only fires interactively. Default: the Messages API with the exact prompt text, same model, named a proxy in CONTRIBUTING; run by the maintainer, not CI.
nodes.norm_label: q8 · how is the type prompt reference run reproducibly

nodes.label: Q9 · What does fail-closed return per gate
nodes.rationale: Default: fail-closed affects PreToolUse only and means ask, never deny; Stop always fail-open; timeout, non-2xx and malformed body all count as API down.
nodes.norm_label: q9 · what does fail-closed return per gate

nodes.label: HG-1 — Run QRSPI on the brief
nodes.rationale: One fresh session per phase, input 00-brief.md; done when 00 to 04 are ticked and the plan passes the zero-context test; its steps become the PRs for HG-2, HG-3, HG-4. Rule 4: the brief does not enter Research.
nodes.norm_label: hg-1 — run qrspi on the brief

nodes.label: HG-10 — Audit mode: log every decision without enforcing
nodes.rationale: Runs both gates for real but always falls through, appending one JSON line per decision to CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA; in 0.1.0 because it is how the thresholds stop being guesses.
nodes.norm_label: hg-10 — audit mode: log every decision without enforcing

nodes.label: HG-11 — Codex CLI adapter: same handlers, Codex answer shape, second manifest
nodes.rationale: Harness from PLUGIN_ROOT, HOOKGATE_HARNESS or stdin shape; permissionDecision allow|deny, ask becomes pass-through with a systemMessage (or codex.askAs: deny); verified live 2026-09-22 on Codex 0.155.1, which dropped plugin-bundled hooks, so hookgate print-hooks writes the repo-level file.
nodes.norm_label: hg-11 — codex cli adapter: same handlers, codex answer shape, second manifest

nodes.label: HG-12 — Per-session decision cache
nodes.rationale: Keyed by session_id and redacted state hash, TTL, invalidated on cwd change; repeat returns under 5 ms with no request and never outlives the session.

nodes.label: HG-13 — Promote confident, repeated decisions into harness rules
nodes.rationale: Three allow or deny answers above 0.95 on one prefix produce one systemMessage proposing the rule in the harness syntax. Propose, never write.
nodes.norm_label: hg-13 — promote confident, repeated decisions into harness rules

nodes.label: HG-14 — hookgate doctor
nodes.rationale: Answers "why is nothing happening"; non-zero only on a broken configuration, never on a slow API.

nodes.label: HG-15 — Screen tool results for injected instructions
nodes.rationale: One Noul on WebFetch, Read and Bash results annotating via additionalContext; off by default until a fixture set gives the false-positive rate.
nodes.norm_label: hg-15 — screen tool results for injected instructions

nodes.label: HG-16 — Benchmark the optimisations: cache, promotion, thresholds
nodes.norm_label: hg-16 — benchmark the optimisations: cache, promotion, thresholds

nodes.label: HG-17 — Say exactly what leaves the machine
nodes.rationale: A plugin that POSTs shell commands and final messages to a third party owes the reader the list per gate, field by field, and what it does not send; check requires the README section.
nodes.norm_label: hg-17 — say exactly what leaves the machine

nodes.label: HG-18 — Bounded, atomic on-disk state
nodes.rationale: The audit log grew without limit and session files were written in place, so racing hooks could tear one. Log rotates at 8 MB; sessions written to temp and renamed, pruned after seven days.

nodes.label: HG-19 — End-to-end tests of the CLI contract
nodes.rationale: HOOKGATE_ENDPOINT (also a proxy hook for users) lets test/e2e.test.mjs spawn the real binary against a fake Jev and assert the JSON, that the session id never leaves, and that a dead endpoint and garbage stdin fail open.
nodes.norm_label: hg-19 — end-to-end tests of the cli contract

nodes.label: HG-2 — Command-risk gate: PreToolUse on Bash answered by Jev
nodes.rationale: One Choice{allow, ask, deny} and one Noul on a redacted, truncated state; below threshold the decision is ask, never allow; a unit test per fail-open path runnable without a key.
nodes.norm_label: hg-2 — command-risk gate: pretooluse on bash answered by jev

nodes.label: HG-20 — CHANGELOG.md
nodes.rationale: Keep a Changelog with HG-n ids on every line; check requires an [Unreleased] section and one for the current version.

nodes.label: HG-21 — Supply chain: CodeQL and pinned actions
nodes.rationale: CodeQL security-extended on push, PR and weekly; Renovate helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests pins every uses: to a digest.
nodes.norm_label: hg-21 — supply chain: codeql and pinned actions

nodes.label: HG-3 — Completion gate: Stop hook that blocks unverified claims of done
nodes.rationale: One Noul on last_assistant_message plus a capped git status; block with a reason naming what to verify; at most one block per stop so the agent cannot loop.
nodes.norm_label: hg-3 — completion gate: stop hook that blocks unverified claims of done

nodes.label: HG-4 — Benchmark: >=50 labelled commands, Jev gate vs type: prompt hook
nodes.rationale: Fundamental: gates the release and every default beyond ask. Under ~90% agreement the command gate ships ask-only. Blocked on a TypeSafe API key since 2026-09-22.
nodes.norm_label: hg-4 — benchmark: >=50 labelled commands, jev gate vs type: prompt hook

nodes.label: HG-5 — First release 0.1.0: trusted publisher, tag, publish
nodes.rationale: Bootstrap done (hookgate@0.0.2 on npm, release.yml proved on its tag); what remains is the trusted publisher and the tag — after HG-4, not before.
nodes.norm_label: hg-5 — first release 0.1.0: trusted publisher, tag, publish

nodes.label: HG-8 — PostToolUse output hygiene (dropped)
nodes.rationale: Dropped: a PostToolUse hook can only add additionalContext or block; it cannot shorten the tool result already in context. A Noul saying "not worth keeping" would add tokens to say something should have been smaller — net negative by construction. Output size is the harness lever; HG-15 keeps the one PostToolUse use that earns a Noul.

nodes.label: HG-9 — Fail-closed as an explicit opt-in
nodes.rationale: failClosed: true means an unreachable API yields ask rather than fall-through; never the default.
nodes.norm_label: hg-9 — fail-closed as an explicit opt-in

nodes.label: Milestone v0.1.0 — Two gates, one benchmark
nodes.rationale: The first release: both gates decided by Jev with calibrated confidence, fail-open, and the reproducible benchmark. Designed through QRSPI under thoughts/HG-1-jev-gates/.
nodes.norm_label: milestone v0.1.0 — two gates, one benchmark

nodes.label: Milestone v0.1.1 — Audit of 2026-09-22
nodes.rationale: A read of the whole tree with a security, privacy and robustness eye the day the gates landed; small items shipped the same day, kept as items so the ids stay in the CHANGELOG.

nodes.label: Milestone v0.2.0 — Observe, promote, port
nodes.rationale: What the first run of the gates teaches, turned into features, plus the second harness the brief designs for.

nodes.label: Benchmark protocol
nodes.rationale: evals/commands.jsonl: 79 commands, 35 safe, 26 ask, 18 dangerous; evals/injection.jsonl: 20 outputs. --baseline runs one claude -p call on claude-opus-5 per command. Runner refuses to start without a key because every run costs money; writes evals/results/<date>-<set>-<jev version>.json. Under ~90% agreement the command gate ships ask-only; the injection screen stays off until zero false positives on the clean set.

nodes.label: Pull request conventions
nodes.rationale: Conventional Commits, HG-n in the subject, a CHANGELOG [Unreleased] line; main protected like qrspi.

nodes.label: Benchmark (not run yet)
nodes.rationale: 79 shell commands labelled safe/ask/dangerous, 20 tool outputs, evals/run.mjs commands --baseline against a type: prompt hook on claude-opus-5; reports agreement, p50/p95 latency, cost per decision and ask share per threshold. One run, one Jev version, dated — a data point, not a suite. Under ~90% agreement the command gate ships ask-only.

nodes.label: hookgate — calibrated, sub-second decisions inside Claude Code hooks
nodes.rationale: Confident: act. Unsure: ask the human. Unreachable: get out of the way. Status: gates implemented, benchmark pending — start in audit mode.
nodes.norm_label: hookgate — calibrated, sub-second decisions inside claude code hooks

nodes.label: Install (Claude Code and Codex CLI)
nodes.rationale: Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add Allan-Nava/hookgate, /plugin install hookgate@hookgate with TYPESAFE_API_KEY. Codex 0.155+ dropped plugin-bundled hooks: npm install -g hookgate; hookgate print-hooks > .codex/hooks.json; Codex asks to trust the hooks file once. Verified live 2026-09-22 with Codex 0.155.1.

nodes.rationale: Ten questions with default assumptions so work can proceed without waiting for answers. Status: generated, not yet reviewed; answers unfilled.

nodes.label: Codex live verification (2026-09-22, Codex 0.155.1)
nodes.rationale: Scratch repo, repo-level .codex/hooks.json, fake Jev on HOOKGATE_ENDPOINT: git push --force → ask at 0.85 → passed through; rm -rf ~/… → deny at 0.97 → blocked; Stop gate ran. Harness detected from stdin shape (turn_id, no prompt_id). Surprises: plugin_hooks removed in this Codex, repo hooks need trust — print-hooks and the README Install section come from that.

nodes.label: HG-1 design notes, as implemented
nodes.rationale: Not QRSPI artifacts: the gates were implemented directly on 2026-09-22 from the brief; these record the decisions taken on the way so the brief and the code agree. HG-1 as a QRSPI run remains the maintainer call.

nodes.label: The benchmark gates the milestone
nodes.rationale: Nothing ships as enforce by default, no threshold moves, and no hookgate--v0.1.0 is tagged before HG-4 has run: the gates decide on a calibration nobody has measured, and a plugin that says deny to a developer had better have a number behind it. Blocked on a TypeSafe API key as of 2026-09-22; audit mode is the only recommended mode until then.

nodes.label: Rule 2: Below threshold is ask, never allow
nodes.rationale: Confidence decides whether to act, the answer decides what; low confidence always lands on the human.
nodes.norm_label: rule 2: below threshold is ask, never allow

nodes.label: Rule 1: Fail-open
nodes.rationale: No key, no network, timeout, 5xx, exception: exit 0, empty stdout, no decision; the harness permission flow takes over. A gate that stalls the agent is worse than none. Fail-closed is an opt-in, never the default.

nodes.label: Rule 7: hookgate narrows, never widens
nodes.rationale: A confident allow passes through by default; only allowMode: "allow" lets the plugin auto-approve, and audit mode never decides. The Stop gate blocks a prompt once, then lets it end.

nodes.label: Fail-open, always
nodes.rationale: No TYPESAFE_API_KEY, no network, a timeout, a 5xx or a bug means no decision: exit 0, empty stdout, normal permission flow applies. A gate that stalls the agent is worse than none. failClosed: true is the explicit opt-in under which an unreachable API makes the command gate ask.

nodes.label: Why in the hooks
nodes.rationale: A harness takes hundreds of small decisions per session, today by static allowlist, a full LLM call (type: prompt hooks — seconds and cents each) or nobody. A System One model fits: unstructured state in, typed answer plus calibrated probability out, no text to parse. TypeSafe covers applications; nobody has put Jev inside the agent harness. That is the gap.

nodes.label: Why not teach Jev?
nodes.rationale: TypeSafe already does, well: official Python and JavaScript SDKs, an MIT plugin with the patterns, thirteen cookbooks. Duplicating that would be noise; hookgate has one job the harness can feel.

nodes.label: Two harnesses, one file (design accounts for Codex from the start)
nodes.rationale: Claude Code in 0.1.0, Codex CLI in 0.2.0; the handler reads the same stdin JSON on both and emits each harness answer shape chosen from the environment (CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT vs PLUGIN_ROOT); two manifests, two hooks.json, no forked logic.
nodes.norm_label: two harnesses, one file (design accounts for codex from the start)

nodes.label: Audit mode is a mode, not a flag per gate
nodes.rationale: Same requests, same thresholds, always fall through, everything logged; the log is the second data source for the benchmark and the only honest way to pick thresholds.
nodes.norm_label: audit mode is a mode, not a flag per gate

nodes.label: Codex is an answer shape, not a fork
nodes.rationale: Detection by PLUGIN_ROOT; ask becomes block with a reason saying to ask the user, because Codex has no ask on PreToolUse. (Note written before the live verification; HG-11 later aligned ask to pass-through plus systemMessage.)
nodes.norm_label: codex is an answer shape, not a fork

nodes.label: Stop guard is double
nodes.rationale: stop_hook_active from the harness plus a per-prompt marker in the session file, so a block can never loop the agent.

nodes.label: HG-8 dropped by construction
nodes.rationale: A hook cannot make a tool result smaller after the fact, only annotate or block; a Noul about "worth keeping" spends tokens to say tokens were wasted. Output hygiene belongs to the harness; the PostToolUse slot goes to injected instructions (HG-15).

nodes.label: Passthrough on allow
nodes.rationale: A PreToolUse allow bypasses the harness own prompt. The Choice is kept as the question, but a confident allow emits no decision by default: hookgate only narrows. allowMode: "allow" opts in once the benchmark says the gate earns it.

nodes.label: Promotion proposes, never writes
nodes.rationale: Three verdicts >= 0.95 on one prefix produce one systemMessage in the detected harness rule syntax, once per prefix per session.

nodes.label: Cache per session, keyed by gate + cwd + redacted state
nodes.rationale: TTL one hour, capped at 500 entries, never shared across sessions: a decision about rm -rf build/ in one repo says nothing about another.
nodes.norm_label: cache per session, keyed by gate + cwd + redacted state

nodes.label: Two questions per command, not one
nodes.rationale: The Choice carries the verdict; a separate Noul on destruction outside the repo is the safety net that turns a confident allow into ask when they disagree. One call answers both.
nodes.norm_label: two questions per command, not one

nodes.label: Errors are typed (JevError.code)
nodes.rationale: JevError.code in no-key, timeout, http, malformed, network; every one ends in fall-through; failClosed turns all but no-key into ask on the command gate only.

nodes.label: Jev API contract (read 2026-09-22)
nodes.rationale: POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone with Bearer TYPESAFE_API_KEY, body {state, model, questions}; question types noul, choice, score; every answer carries confidence 0-1. Model jev-1.13.0, aliases jev-latest/jev-preview; limits 64k per request, 32k state; $42 per billion input tokens; errors 401, 422, 429, 529.

nodes.label: qrspi (sibling project)
nodes.rationale: The project hookgate is modelled on: a Markdown-first plugin, a dependency-free installer, a site generated from the README, releases by tag.

nodes.label: Constraints: state <= 32k tokens, 2 s latency budget
nodes.rationale: Truncate commands and messages; redact secret-looking values; explicit timeout, Jev promises 70-500 ms.
nodes.norm_label: constraints: state <= 32k tokens, 2 s latency budget

nodes.label: Done-when criteria
nodes.rationale: Plugin installable in any repo; PreToolUse on Bash returns allow|ask|deny with a reason; Stop returns block; fail-open on missing key; reproducible benchmark in evals/ with >=50 labelled commands; npm test validates manifests; CI on Node 18/20/22/24; release by tag as in qrspi.

nodes.label: Open risks (Codex ask, Jev calibration, jev-latest drift)
nodes.rationale: Codex has no ask on PreToolUse; Jev calibration on shell-command risk is unmeasured — under ~90% agreement the command gate stays ask-only; jev-latest can change answers, so the benchmark re-runs at every version.
nodes.norm_label: open risks (codex ask, jev calibration, jev-latest drift)

nodes.label: hookgate — Claude Code (and Codex) plugin
nodes.rationale: Whole product is two hook handlers, PreToolUse on Bash and Stop, answered by TypeSafe Jev with calibrated confidence; both escalate to the human when confidence is low. Modelled on qrspi: dependency-free, one installer, manifests in step, releases by tag.

nodes.rationale: The check validates manifests and versions, hooks.json, the fail-open statement in the README and the tarball files; extend it whenever an invariant is added.

nodes.label: HG-1 brief — Jev in Claude Code gates
nodes.rationale: Brief from an interview on 2026-09-22; the input to the Questions phase. Goal: the small, frequent harness decisions taken by Jev in ~100 ms with calibrated confidence instead of an LLM or nobody.

nodes.label: Rule 3: State never carries secrets
nodes.rationale: Redact token-looking values before the request; truncate to Jev 32k-token state limit.

nodes.label: Rule 4: Zero runtime dependencies, Node 18+
nodes.rationale: A hook runs on every tool call; one fetch to POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone; check fails on a dependencies block.

nodes.label: Why zero dependencies?
nodes.rationale: A hook starts on every tool call. Start-up cost is the cost, so nothing to install, nothing to resolve, one file to read.

nodes.label: Decision: gates in the harness, not a library for apps
nodes.rationale: Because that is the gap: TypeSafe covers apps.
nodes.norm_label: decision: gates in the harness, not a library for apps

nodes.label: Decision: name hookgate
nodes.rationale: Free on npm and GitHub on 2026-09-22, describes the thing; uses neither Jev nor TypeSafe, their marks.

nodes.label: Decision: new public repo, npm, the qrspi operating model
nodes.rationale: Because qrspi stays Markdown-only and does not tie its thesis to a vendor.
nodes.norm_label: decision: new public repo, npm, the qrspi operating model

nodes.label: Decision: zero dependencies, native fetch
nodes.rationale: A hook starts on every tool call and must cost nothing at start-up; Node 18 has fetch.

nodes.label: Backlog issue sync (one-way)
nodes.rationale: BACKLOG.md is the single source of truth; issues are a view of it. Sync runs one way only, backlog to issues, never the reverse: editing or closing an issue on GitHub changes nothing, ticking the item in BACKLOG.md does. Runs only when BACKLOG.md, the script or the workflow change, plus on demand with dry_run. A concurrency group prevents two racing runs opening HG-n twice; the plan is printed before apply so the log says what it was about to do.

nodes.label: CI backlog job (lint, check, planner test)
nodes.rationale: A stale ROADMAP.md fails here; the planner decisions are asserted against a fixture because a wrong decision opens duplicates or closes open work on a public repository.
nodes.norm_label: ci backlog job (lint, check, planner test)

nodes.label: Release drift check
nodes.rationale: A merged release PR publishes nothing: the tag is the trigger and pushing it is manual. qrspi 0.1.1 sat on main untagged for a week and nothing said so. Fails when package.json version has no hookgate--v<version> tag once the commit that set it is older than a 2 h grace; runs on push and daily so a failing scheduled run emails the owner.

nodes.label: Close the milestone step
nodes.rationale: Closes the open milestone whose title starts with v<version> only when it has zero open issues; otherwise warns and leaves it open.

nodes.label: Release pipeline (on tag hookgate--v*)
nodes.rationale: Triggered by the tag claude plugin tag creates. Verifies tag version equals package.json, pins npm@11.19.0 (npm@latest would be a moving dependency in the publishing path), installs with --ignore-scripts because the job holds the OIDC privilege, publishes, waits up to five minutes (20 x 15 s) for the registry, creates the GitHub release and closes the milestone. Every step is rerun-safe.

nodes.label: Backlog, roadmap, issues workflow
nodes.rationale: The planner is tested against scripts/fixtures/ without a network call because its failure modes are all decisions: a duplicate opened on every push, an issue closed for open work.

nodes.label: Release runbook
nodes.rationale: Bump the three manifests, npm test, land through a PR, then claude plugin tag . --push; the tag triggers release.yml; failed runs re-run with gh workflow run Release -f tag=…; every step idempotent.

nodes.label: One-time npm Trusted Publisher setup
nodes.rationale: First version published by hand, then on npmjs.com configure GitHub Actions publisher: user Allan-Nava, repo hookgate, workflow release.yml, environment empty. Never rename release.yml; never give setup-node a registry-url.

nodes.label: ROADMAP.md (generated view by milestone)
nodes.rationale: Generated by scripts/backlog.mjs roadmap from BACKLOG.md; do not edit by hand; CI fails when the two disagree. 21 items, 16 shipped, 5 open, 3 milestones.

nodes.label: Backlog planner fixture (v9.9.0)
nodes.rationale: Six HG items covering each planner decision: open with issue, open without, open with closed issue, shipped with open issue, shipped that never had one, open retitled.

nodes.label: Skip already-published version (bootstrap)
nodes.rationale: npm forbids configuring a trusted publisher for a package that does not exist, so the very first version is published by hand; the job skips publish when the version is already on the registry but still cuts the release and closes the milestone.

nodes.label: npm Trusted Publishing over OIDC
nodes.rationale: No npm token anywhere: publish authenticates through OIDC bound to the literal workflow filename release.yml — DO NOT RENAME. setup-node must get no registry-url: it writes an .npmrc with a placeholder _authToken, npm sees a configured credential and skips the OIDC exchange, answering 404 not 401. NODE_AUTH_TOKEN is unset belt-and-braces. Provenance is automatic so --provenance is not passed.

nodes.label: BACKLOG.md as single source of truth
nodes.rationale: Every planned item has a stable HG-n id so commits, CHANGELOG, thoughts/ artifacts and issues can reference it. ROADMAP.md and the GitHub issues are generated views; new ideas go here rather than scattered TODOs.
nodes.norm_label: backlog.md as single source of truth

nodes.rationale: hookgate on npm carried a 0.0.1 published and unpublished from this account on 2026-03-23; npm never lets a version be reused, so the first publishable version is 0.0.2. npm view reports an error for a name with no live versions, which reads as free — check the registry JSON time.unpublished instead.
